Customization Guide
How to Customize Lobby Colors
Learn how to edit your lobby appearance by changing host text, host colors,
icons, player name colors, and tag styling inside your language file.
This version starts with simple solid-color examples first.
Before You Start
When you first download the mod, you will usually see a
template.dat file in your language folder. To use it,
rename template.dat to english.dat,
then open it and fill in the values you want to customize.
Steam\steamapps\common\Among Us\Language
Always make a backup before editing your file. If something breaks,
restore the backup and try again.
Step 1: Go to your
Among Us (Mod)\Language folder.
Step 2: Find template.dat.
Step 3: Rename it to english.dat.
Step 4: Open the file in a text editor and fill in your values.
Step 5: Save the file and then press F5 + T.

Beginner
Solid Colors First
If you are new to this, start here. Solid colors are the easiest to test
because each line only uses one hex color code. Once this works, you can
move on to more advanced styling later.
Flat color values
HostColor: / IconColor: / NameColor:
These use normal hex color codes like
#3A86FF, #8338EC, or #06D6A0.
HostColor:#3A86FF
IconColor:#8338EC
NameColor:#06D6A0
Simple host text
HostText:
This colors the entire word using one color.
HostText:<color=#3A86FF>Host</color>
Host icon
Icon:
Changes the symbol next to the host name.
Try symbols like ★ ✿ ◆ ♣
Icon:★
Intermediate
Gradient Wrapping
Gradients work by wrapping each letter in its own
<color=...> tag and slowly changing the hex code from
one letter to the next. That is what gives the text a smooth fade instead
of one flat solid color.
Basic idea
Start with a short word first. Each letter gets its own color tag, and
the colors should move in a gentle order instead of jumping around.
HostText:<color=#FF6B6B>M</color><color=#FF8E53>A</color><color=#FFD166>U</color><color=#22C55E>L</color>
Admin tag example
Admin and staff tags work the same way: color one character at a
time so the tag fades smoothly instead of jumping between shades.
AdminTag:<color=#FF2D2D>A</color><color=#E11D48>d</color><color=#BE123C>m</color><color=#991B1B>i</color><color=#7F1D1D>n</color>
If a gradient looks messy, reduce the number of colors and test a smaller
word first. Clean 3 to 5 color blends usually look better than using too
many random shades.
Quick Tips
Use hex colors like #3A86FF, #8338EC, or #06D6A0.
Solid colors are easier to create and debug than gradients.
Wrap each letter in its own <color=...> tag for more advanced styling.
Keep a backup of both template.dat and english.dat.
If the game does not update right away, save the file then click F5 + T.
Copy working examples first, then change colors one step at a time.
If your game language is another language be sure to set the file to (your language.dat).
You may need to run a round in order to populate the language file depenidng on the mod.
You can change roles or taglines, not just color. If you`re familiar with my lobbies Gatitos > VIP Gatos > Mod for example.

pages.text:
Join MAUL
Player + Host Quick Reference
Modded Among Us FAQ
A general how-to page for players and hosts.
Player Help
Host Help
Join Faster
Learn what modded regions are, when you need one, and the quickest way for mobile and PC players to join.
Host Cleaner
Keep a short checklist for updating the mod, enabling autostart, queue tools, and handling known lobby issues.
Add Custom Tags
Learn about adding custom tags to your mod if it supports them, then place the finished file in the correct data folder.
Fix Problems
Use the black-screen fix, the Niko region notes, and the log tools before assuming the mod is broken.
For Players
New to Modded Among Us? Start here. These are the questions players usually ask first.
What is Modded Among Us?
Modded Among Us is not just impostors versus crewmates anymore. Games can include impostors, crewmates,
coven roles, neutrals, and add-ons all in the same match.
Depending on the mod, you may also get access to mini-games like FFA.
The five big role groups to remember are Impostors, Crewmates,
Neutrals, Coven, and Add-ons. That is why kills,
votes, and suspicious behavior do not always mean the same thing they do in vanilla.
In modded Among Us, crew can kill too.
Do I need to install the mod to join a lobby?
For standard host-only lobbies, the host is the one who must have the mod installed. Players can
usually join without installing the mod themselves.
However, some mods like Town of Us Mira may require players to install the mod too. Those can be installed
on PC or Android with
Starlight Launcher.
What is a modded region?
A modded region is a non-Innersloth region that helps mods run when the official anti-cheat breaks
lobbies. If you are experiencing host errors like banned for hacking or repeated kicks and the issue is
widespread, swapping to a modded region may be a good alternative.
Niko regions are commonly suggested for host-only mods like EHR or Project Lotus. More general modded
regions are commonly suggested for client-required mods like Town of Us.
These regions can be installed on mobile, tablet, or PC.
How do I join a modded region on mobile?
Open Among Us.
Open mauq.xyz/servers or au.niko233.top.
Pick the region your host is using, such as Niko NA or Niko EU.
Tap it and let it open Among Us again.
For good measure, go back to the link and tap your region one more time, then let it open Among Us again.
Click Create a Game.
Open the region selector and check if Niko regions are now listed.
Select the correct region if it is there.
Go back to the main screen and join the host's lobby.
How do I join a modded region on PC?
If you already have the mod installed, modded regions typically come along with the mod. If not, visit
au.niko233.top and run the
customserver.bat file.
Error or domain issue?
Delete MiniRegionInstall from BepInEx/plugins.
Download the custom server BAT file.
Launch the file.
Press the button it asks for.
Relaunch the game.
Which commands should I learn first?
These are the most useful basics for regular players:
/m or /cmd m to read your role and add-on details.
/r to list active roles, or /r [role] to read one role.
/id or /cmd id to see player IDs.
/kc or /cmd kc to see how many killers are still alive.
/death or /cmd d after death to see death information.
/w [ids] [message] for meeting whispers when your role allows it.
In meetings, use the /cmd prefix for guessing, whispering, judging, and other hidden role
actions so you do not expose yourself in public chat.
How does guessing work?
Use /cmd id to find the player's ID.
In the meeting, use /cmd bt [ID] [RoleName].
Typically the mod will show a player's ID on their meeting card, but if it does not, you can run
/id beforehand to get it.
Example: Sarha is Dictator and I am an impostor, so I want to remove her before she removes me.
I would use /bt 0 dictator.
Modded clients also have a guesser UI in most mods that makes guessing easier, so check for that in meetings.
Why do I keep getting guessed?
There are a few reasons. Experienced players learn common role tells over time, especially when a newer
player gives away what they are doing.
Even if you never say your role name out loud, people can infer it from system messages, how you ask
questions, or what commands you use. Something like asking how to get a player's ID and then immediately
using a meeting command can give you away.
If you need help, it is usually safer to run /m in game to learn your role, or ask whether
guessing is on before you start doing obvious role-specific actions.
If your role color matches another visible player, you are often on the same team. Do not guess or kill
teammates unless your instructions say otherwise.
You may also see icons next to someone's name. You can run /icons in game to check what
they mean. In some cases you could be somebody's lawyer and need to protect them, or they could be an
Executioner's target.
What if I die?
Do not leave. Some roles can still win after death, some ghost roles activate after death, and ghost
chat is still useful. Leaving early can also make you miss role information that matters later.
A kill does not always mean evil. Crew killing roles like Sheriff, Vigilante, or Crusader can exist.
If your role and name color match another visible player, you are often on the same team. Do not guess or kill teammates unless your instructions say otherwise.
If you froze, black-screened, lost chat, or could not vote, it may be role-related rather than a normal game glitch.
Use /m in game before asking public role questions. It is one of the easiest ways to avoid getting guessed early.
Information taken and/or inspired by @RoHodor's EHR guide.
For Hosts
These are the most common questions for hosts who use mods.
How do I update the mod normally?
Download the newest mod DLL and replace the old one in Among Us/BepInEx/plugins.
For example, with EHR test builds:
Open BepInEx.
Open plugins.
Delete the old EHR.dll.
Paste the new EHR.dll in.
What are good autohost settings?
Initial countdown: about 10 seconds.
Delay before entering: about 5 to 10 seconds.
Forced start: around 1.5 to 3.
Minutes before autostart: around 1.5 to 2.
Enable Autostart in the mod settings behind the gear icon.
If you plan to be AFK, do not forget to enable Game Master.
How do queue and code tools work in MAUQ?
/thread rename to rename a lobby thread.
/thread close to archive and lock a lobby post.
/code set to set the private code.
/queue toggle to turn queue on or off.
/queue next to ping the next players and send the code.
/queue remove to remove someone without pinging them.
/code remove then /code set to change the code.
/blacklist toggle (member) to add someone to the blacklist.
More advanced queue settings can be found on
mauq.xyz.
What is the current known host ban or kick issue?
The current workarounds are:
Play with 9 or fewer users.
Stick to mini-games that do not have a kill button.
Use Niko regions as mentioned above.
How do I read logs when something breaks?
Use these tools before guessing at the problem:
EHR Log Analyzer for EHR logs.
MAUQ Log Reader for other mod logs.
Custom Tags
How does everyone have pretty names in Among Us? I want one too.
1
Create the tag
Go to
moddedamong.us/tags,
fill out the form, and download the generated .txt file. Make sure you enter
your friend code.
2
Send it to the host
After downloading the file, send that .txt file to the lobby host.
3
Name it correctly
The host must make sure the filename exactly matches the player friend code, for example
friendcode#1234.txt.
4
Place it in the data folder
Move the file into the mod user-data folder. For EHR, for example:
EHR-Data > User-data > friendcode#1234.txt.
Custom tags are host- and mod-dependent, so exact setup can differ between mods.
The filename must match the friend code exactly or the tag may not load.
In EHR, hosts can also use /addtag and /deletetag, but that is separate from the file-based method above.
Quick Command Reference
These are the commands most worth memorizing for basic play, meetings, and hosting. The full command list is much longer. These are general commands, though some are more EHR-specific.
Any Time
/id show player IDs
/r show active roles
/r [role] show one role description
/h or /help list commands
/template send a saved template
Lobby
/color [color] change bean color
/tpout leave the ship area
/tpin return to the ship
/l or /lastresult view the last game
/win view the last winners
Meeting
/cmd m read your role details
/cmd kc see how many killers remain
/cmd bt [id] [role] guess a role
/w [ids] [message] whisper privately
/cmd d see death info after death
Host Tools
/setrole or /setaddon set next-game roles
/combo force or ban role plus add-on combos
/readycheck run an AFK check
/draftstart start role drafting
/addtag add a host-managed tag
Common Support Topics
These are some of the most commonly asked support questions.
How do I downgrade Among Us for the mod?
Steam: open Among Us in Steam, go to Properties, then Betas, and choose public-previous.
After downgrading on Steam or Epic, you should delete
%userprofile%\AppData\LocalLow\Innersloth\Among Us\settings.amogus to avoid black screens.
If you use Steam, be sure to copy your newly downgraded Among Us files into the mod folder that you use.
I got kicked for domain mismatch. What do I do now?
Use au.niko233.top.
Niko233.me now causes immediate kicks because of the domain migration check.
I am on a guest account and cannot join Niko servers.
Guest accounts are not supported. An account is required.
I have terrible connectivity or cross-region lag.
Try using Cloudflare WARP for stability.
I keep getting kicked as soon as I create a lobby.
When you click Create a Game, check how many players you have set and make sure it is
15 or under. You can also open a local lobby and check how many impostors you have set.
How do I install a mod on Linux?
Requirements: own Among Us on Steam and have some patience.
Open Steam and go to your library, then select Among Us.
Click the gear icon, choose Manage, then Browse Local Files.
Download the mod you want for Steam.
Unzip the mod files and paste them into the Among Us folder you opened.
Open a terminal and run sudo apt update, sudo apt install pipx, then pipx ensurepath.
Restart the terminal.
Run pipx install protontricks.
Launch Among Us once, wait for it to load, then close it.
Run protontricks 945360 winhttp.
Back in Steam, open Properties for Among Us.
In General, set launch options to WINEDLLOVERRIDES="winhttp=n,b" %command%.
In Compatibility, force a specific Steam Play tool and choose Proton Experimental.
Relaunch the game.
The first launch after setup can take 2 to 3 minutes.
Common Among Us error messages
Common errors and their usual causes:
Sent # pings that remote has not responded to: usually weak network connection. Try restarting your connection or moving to a stronger signal.
ReliablePacketWithoutResponse: often server traffic or unstable connection. Restarting can help.
Network is unreachable: usually weak internet, especially mobile data. Try Wi-Fi or stronger signal.
You are running an older version of the game: update or downgrade to the version the lobby is using.
Could not find the game you're looking for: the code may be wrong, the lobby may have closed, or the region may not match.
SteamworksAuthFail or AuthFail: Steam or the matching platform may not be open correctly in the background.
Bad Gateway or authentication errors: often server-side. Restarting can help, but sometimes you just have to wait.
Network Packet Loss or Reliable packet was not ack'd: usually unstable connection or region mismatch. Changing regions can help.

Highlighted Users · Badges · Requirements
Featured Users
Featured Users showcase the people who help make MAUL special
hosts, developers, contributors, helpers, staff, creators, and more.
If you think you qualify, check the requirements below and apply through the correct route.
Home
Join MAUL
The Featured Users section highlights trusted, active, and notable members of the MAUL community.
This includes Verified Hosts, returning hosts, community helpers, server staff, mod developers,
major contributors, content creators, and users with standout activity, loyalty, or consistency.
If you believe you qualify, please follow the application instructions below and contact
Sarha
if needed.
Verified Host Perks
Being a Verified Host comes with extra recognition and useful server permissions.
Lobby Posting Access
Can post and ping in verified-host-lobbies as the host.
Event Hosting
Can hold events in the Event section/category.
Custom Role
Can create a custom role using @Booster Bot.
VC Assignment
Can assign @Blacklisted VC.
Exclusive Access
Access to the Verified Host category and exclusive-chat.
Server Recognition
Displayed as an officially recognized MAUL host with a dedicated featured badge/status.
Featured User Badges
These are the badge categories currently used for Featured Users. Badge appearance may vary, and some are tied
to specific recognition, activity, region, or hosting milestones.
Tester / Bug Hunter
For users who test features, report bugs, or help catch issues affecting mods, systems, or community tools.
Developer
For mod developers or known community bot developers recognized within the modded Among Us space.
Contributor
For users who contribute to a mod or a known community bot through code, ideas, testing, assets, or support.
Newest VH
Highlights the newest member added to the Verified Host lineup.
Verified Host
Main Verified Host recognition badge. This may later be replaced or expanded with numbered badges.
Lobby Milestones
Flame badges mark amount of lobbies hosted, including 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400, and 500+ lobbies.
Helper
For members active in support or welcome-chat and known for helping others.
Staff
For official MAUL server staff members.
Booster
For members who have boosted the server for 3+ months.
Large / Trusted Server Owner
For owners of large or trusted servers recognized by the community.
Large / Trusted Server Admin
For admins of large or trusted servers recognized by the community.
Returning / OG Host
For hosts who were active prior to 2024 and returned, or long-time OG hosts.
Hosts EHR the Most
Recognition for the user most associated with hosting Endless Host Roles.
Hosts Project Lotus the Most
Recognition for the user most associated with hosting Project Lotus.
Hosts TOUM the Most
Recognition for the user most associated with hosting TOUM.
Hosts MGM the Most
Recognition for the user most associated with hosting MGM.
Most Active Chatter
For standout chat activity and consistent community engagement.
Content Creator / Contributor
For recognized creators or contributors making community content, media, guides, or promotional material.
Most Consistent Host
For hosts who show strong long-term consistency and reliability in their lobby schedule.
Event Host
For users who have hosted an event in MAUL.
Veteran User
Recognizes duration of time in the server or being a Verified Host for x amount of years.
Region Badges
Region-based recognition for North America, Europe, and Asia.
How to Apply
Developers, staff, Level 175+, and Verified Hosts can apply through the proper channel.
Users who meet these requirements can
DM Sarha
or open a
ticket.
Contact Sarha
Open a Ticket
Featured User qualifications, perks, badges, and requirements may change over time.
Final decisions are handled through MAUL staff and the Featured User review process.

Privacy Policy & Terms of Service
Modded Among Us Mafia
This page explains what data the Modded Among Us Mafia Discord bot uses, why it is used,
how long it may be kept, and the basic rules for using the bot's Mafia systems in
Modded Among Us Lobbies.
Contact Admin
@sarhadactyl
Priority Tickets
Bot
Modded Among Us Mafia, Discord application ID 1530443638809563236.

What The Bot Does
Modded Among Us Mafia is a Discord community bot used to run and manage the Mafia systems that
were previously handled by the Modded Among Us Games bot.
Mafia Game Management
The bot supports Mafia setup, player joining, host controls, role assignment, private game
channels or chats, game logs, voting, night actions, points, stats, mutes, warnings, FAQ panels,
and staff review workflows related to Mafia games.
Server-Only Use
The bot is intended for Modded Among Us Lobbies and related Mafia workflows. It is not a public
multipurpose bot, and it is not used to sell user data or serve advertising.
Information We Collect
The bot only collects or processes Discord information needed for enabled Mafia features,
server administration, support, safety, and troubleshooting.
Discord Account And Server Data
Discord user IDs, usernames, display names, avatars, and mentions.
Server IDs, channel IDs, thread IDs, role IDs, message IDs, and application IDs.
Member role information and permissions when needed for Mafia hosts, staff controls, eligibility checks, or private channel access.
Invite, join, leave, nickname, or server event details when used by Mafia staff safety or review tools.
Mafia Feature Data
Game setup, host information, joined players, assigned roles, alive or eliminated status, team or alignment data, and game outcomes.
Votes, night actions, private chat or channel IDs, logs, moderation notes, warnings, mutes, points, host stats, and game statistics.
Server configuration such as enabled cogs, command settings, staff roles, logging channels, game settings, and FAQ or panel settings.
Command usage, timestamps, errors, diagnostics, and limited interaction content needed to process commands, buttons, menus, and modals.
How We Use Information
Operational Use
Information is used to run Mafia games, manage hosts and players, assign or restrict roles,
maintain private game spaces, process votes and actions, show results, track optional stats,
and save server settings chosen by authorized staff.
Safety And Abuse Prevention
Information may also be used to prevent cheating, command abuse, spam, duplicate actions,
moderation evasion, unauthorized access to private Mafia areas, or misuse of server systems.
Discord Gateway Intents
The bot uses Discord gateway intents so Discord can send events needed for commands, Mafia game
operation, moderation, staff tools, private channels, logs, role checks, and support workflows.
Message Content Intent
Used when message text is needed for prefix commands, host commands, Mafia game log parsing,
private chat workflows, moderation tools, staff notes, FAQ responses, and other chat-based
Mafia features.
Server Members Intent
Used to read member information needed for role checks, host permissions, private game access,
mutes, warnings, nickname enforcement, participation tracking, staff review, and member support.
Default Discord Events
Used for normal server operation, such as knowing which servers, channels, threads, roles,
messages, reactions, voice states, invites, emojis, and interactions exist where the bot has
permission. These events support commands, panels, logs, reactions, and Mafia automation.
Feature And Cog Examples
Known Mafia-related examples from the previous bot include:
Mafia panel and command tools (cogs.mafiapanel,
cogs.mafiacommands, cogs.mafiaauto, and
cogs.mafiafaqpanel) process command metadata, interactions, roles, channels,
threads, messages, and game configuration for Mafia setup and operation.
Mafia private spaces (cogs.mafia_private_chats) process member,
role, channel, thread, and message information to create or manage private Mafia chats or
channels.
Mafia host, points, and records (cogs.mafia_host_tracking,
cogs.mafia_points, and cogs.maulmafia) process game participation,
host records, point totals, game results, and related statistics.
Mafia moderation and staff safety (cogs.mafia_mutes,
cogs.mafia_warnings, cogs.maulnotes, cogs.ncic,
cogs.punishments, cogs.warn, cogs.banemoji,
cogs.skull_ban, and cogs.rename) process member, role, invite,
reaction, nickname, thread, and message data for safety, logs, notes, warnings, mutes,
punishments, and staff review.
Message Content
Why Message Content Is Used
The bot may read message content in server channels where it has access when message content is
required for enabled Mafia features. This includes prefix commands, host commands, Mafia logs,
vote or action parsing, private game chat workflows, staff notes, and chat-based moderation.
Limits
Message content is used for bot functionality only. It is not sold, used for advertising, or
shared with unrelated third parties. The bot is not intended to monitor or store unrelated server
conversations.
Storage And Access
Where Data Is Stored
Bot data may be stored in local databases, configuration files, logs, or other storage used to
operate the bot. Stored data may include Mafia game records, points, host records, moderation
records, server settings, warnings, mutes, staff notes, and user opt-in or participation data.
Who Can Access It
Access is limited to authorized server staff, bot maintainers, or administrators who need the
information to operate, moderate, troubleshoot, or maintain the bot and server.
Retention And Deletion
Retention
Active Mafia game data is kept as long as needed to run the game and clean up after it ends.
Server configuration, optional stats, game history, moderation history, audit logs, and
abuse-prevention records may be kept while needed for server administration or safety.
Deletion Requests
Users may request deletion of eligible stored data. Server owners or authorized administrators
may request deletion of server-linked configuration or records. Some data may be retained when
needed for moderation history, safety, unresolved disputes, audit logs, or abuse prevention.
Sharing
No Sale Of Data
We do not sell user data. We do not share collected data with advertisers or unrelated third
parties.
Normal Server Visibility
Some bot output may be visible in server channels as part of normal functionality, such as game
signups, host panels, results, logs, public stats, warnings, point totals, or participation
information.
Terms Of Service
By adding, using, or interacting with Modded Among Us Mafia, you agree to these Terms of Service.
If you do not agree, do not use the bot and remove it from your server if you have permission to do so.
Allowed Use
Use the bot only for lawful Discord server gameplay, moderation, support, and Mafia administration.
Do not use the bot to harass, threaten, abuse, spam, raid, scam, phish, or distribute malicious content.
Do not exploit, disrupt, overload, reverse engineer, or bypass limits in the bot.
Do not use the bot in a way that violates Discord's rules, applicable law, or the rules of the server where it is installed.
Do not misrepresent the bot as being owned, operated, endorsed, or approved by Discord or InnerSloth.
Server Responsibility
Server owners and administrators are responsible for deciding whether the bot is appropriate for
their server, configuring it safely, assigning suitable permissions, and making sure bot use
follows Discord's Terms of Service, Discord's Community Guidelines, and server rules.
Availability And Changes
The bot is provided as available. Features may be changed, paused, limited, or removed at any
time, including Mafia cogs, commands, settings, statistics, game modes, and support features.
We may restrict or block access for users or servers that abuse the bot, create security risks,
or violate these terms.
No Warranty And Liability Limits
The bot is provided without warranties of any kind. To the fullest extent allowed by law, the bot
operator is not liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, or
for loss of data, server disruption, game disruption, or user disputes arising from use of the bot.
Relationship To Discord Terms
Use of the bot also depends on Discord's own services, rules, permissions, and platform behavior.
Nothing on this page replaces or overrides Discord's Terms of Service, Discord's Privacy Policy, the
Discord Developer Terms of Service, or the Discord Developer Policy. If there is a conflict,
Discord's applicable terms control your use of Discord and the Discord API.

Discord Bot Privacy Policy
Modded Among Us Games
This privacy policy explains what data the Modded Among Us Games Discord bot uses, why it is used,
how it is stored, and how members can contact us about privacy requests.
Contact Admin
@sarhadactyl
Priority Tickets
Bot
Modded Among Us Games, Discord application ID 1291220895846760523.
Server
Used for the Modded Among Us Lobbies community and its server systems.
Owner
Managed by
@sarhadactyl.
Updated
Effective June 11, 2026. Last updated July 11, 2026.
What The App Does
Modded Among Us Games is a private Discord community bot used to support and automate the Modded
Among Us Lobbies server.
Community Management
The bot helps staff and members with moderation, role management, verification-related workflows,
giveaways, events, minigames, Mafia and Among Us community tools, host tracking, warning systems,
member support, server notifications, and activity tracking.
Server-Only Use
The bot is intended for use within Modded Among Us Lobbies and related community workflows. It is
not a public multipurpose bot and is not used to sell user data or serve advertising.
Information We Collect
The bot only collects or processes Discord information needed for its enabled features.
Discord Account And Server Data
Discord user IDs, usernames, display names, and mentions.
Server IDs, channel IDs, thread IDs, role IDs, message IDs, and application IDs.
Member role information and server join dates when needed for permissions, panels, or eligibility checks.
Invite-related information when needed for member access or invite tracking workflows.
Bot Feature Data
Giveaway entries, eligibility checks, bonus entries, reroll records, and giveaway audit logs.
Moderation records such as warnings, mutes, punishments, staff notes, role changes, and audit entries.
Game, event, Mafia, host, and participation statistics.
Economy and minigame data, including balances, inventory, rewards, cooldowns, participation, and transaction logs.
User opt-in preferences for role panels, notifications, pings, stream alerts, and related features.
PingMe / DCD lobby notification settings, subscriber lists, forum thread settings, and optional thread emoji suffixes.
How We Use Information
Operational Use
Information is used to run commands, manage roles, enforce server requirements, support moderation,
operate giveaways, track game hosting, run minigames, manage server notifications, and maintain
server configuration.
Safety And Abuse Prevention
Information may also be used to prevent spam, duplicate entries, cheating, command abuse,
moderation evasion, or misuse of server systems.
Discord Gateway Intents
The bot uses Discord gateway intents so Discord can send events needed for commands, moderation,
role systems, notifications, and lobby tools. The bot uses Discord's default intents plus the
privileged message content, server members, and presence intents.
Message Content Intent
Used when message text is needed for prefix commands, custom commands, autoresponders, sticky
messages, Mafia or game log parsing, chat activity tracking, economy rewards, moderation tools,
and other chat-based server features.
Server Members Intent
Used to read member information needed for verification-related workflows, role panels, role
management, permission checks, moderation actions, warning systems, eligibility checks,
participation tracking, and member support tools.
Presence Intent
Used for features that depend on Discord activity status, especially Among Us rich presence. This
lets the bot detect when a tracked host appears to be in an open lobby, post lobby-open messages,
ping opted-in members, and show a user's current activity details through debug commands.
Default Discord Events
Used for normal server operation, such as knowing which servers, channels, threads, roles,
messages, reactions, voice states, invites, emojis, and interactions exist where the bot has
permission. These events support commands, panels, logs, reaction features, voice or lobby tools,
and server automation.
Feature And Cog Examples
Known examples from the current workspace and supplied cog archive include:
Element Tribes (cogs.element_tribes /
cogs.ElementTribes) processes message, member, reaction, voice, thread, and
interaction events for tribe assignment, chat and voice objectives, custom quests, Harmony
submissions, reaction quests, command tracking, panels, and staff review workflows.
Verification, role, and access tools (cogs.verification_role_swap,
cogs.verify_sqlite, cogs.verify_mysql,
cogs.verify_fallback, cogs.verify_followup,
cogs.role_management, cogs.gamepanel,
cogs.internationalpanel, and cogs.forum_threads) process member,
role, message, thread, and interaction events for verification prompts, role swaps, role
panels, game/access roles, forum access, and follow-up verification support.
Message, command, help, and responder tools (cogs.amongus,
cogs.amongus_help, cogs.auhelp, cogs.customtags,
cogs.MAULtag, cogs.quote, cogs.type,
cogs.translation, cogs.banned_responder, cogs.delete,
cogs.guildmanager, cogs.starlightcv2,
cogs.FeaturedMod, cogs.adminusertools, and
cogs.dashboard_deploy) process message content, command metadata, channel/thread
data, and member permissions for prefix commands, help responses, custom tags, translations,
moderation utilities, and dashboard or responder workflows.
Economy, leveling, games, and event tools (cogs.beans,
cogs.leveling, cogs.giveaways, cogs.EasterHunt,
cogs.bombevent, cogs.valentine, cogs.autoreact,
cogs.upvotes, cogs.skullboard, and
cogs.reaction_logger) process message, reaction, member, role, voice, and thread
events for rewards, participation, leaderboards, giveaway eligibility, reaction logging,
event progress, and anti-abuse checks.
Lobby, voice, presence, stream, and timer tools (cogs.pingme,
cogs.vc_lobby_tracker, cogs.vc_bcl_hosting_leaderboard,
cogs.MobileLobby, cogs.no_among_us, cogs.status,
cogs.blvc, cogs.streamping, and cogs.lmstimer) process
presence, voice state, member, channel, thread, and role events to detect Among Us lobby
activity, track hosts, create or update lobby posts, restrict voice access, run timers, and
notify opted-in members.
Mafia, moderation, and staff safety tools (cogs.mafiapanel,
cogs.mafiacommands, cogs.mafiaauto,
cogs.mafia_host_tracking, cogs.mafia_private_chats,
cogs.mafia_points, cogs.mafia_mutes,
cogs.mafia_warnings, cogs.mafiafaqpanel,
cogs.maulmafia, cogs.maulnotes, cogs.ncic,
cogs.punishments, cogs.warn, cogs.banemoji,
cogs.skull_ban, and cogs.rename) process message, member, role,
invite, reaction, and thread events for Mafia logs, private game channels, host stats, points,
mutes, warnings, invite history, member join/leave records, nickname enforcement, and staff
review tools.
Scheduling and community utilities (cogs.calendar,
cogs.birthday, cogs.sticky, and related panel utilities) process
member, role, channel, message, thread, and interaction events for event reminders, birthday
features, sticky messages, panels, and server organization.
Message Content
Why Message Content Is Used
The bot may read message content in server channels where it has access when message content is
required for enabled features. This includes prefix commands, custom commands, autoresponders,
sticky messages, Mafia or game log parsing, chat activity tracking, economy rewards, and chat-based
minigames.
Limits
Message content is used for bot functionality only. It is not sold, used for advertising, or shared
with unrelated third parties.
Presence And Activity Data
Lobby Notifications
The bot may use Discord presence or activity data for features that detect relevant game or lobby
states, such as Among Us lobby reopen notifications. This allows opted-in members to receive
useful pings when a tracked lobby becomes available.
Activity Debugging
Presence information may also be shown to a user through debugging commands so they can verify
whether Discord is exposing the activity needed for lobby notification features.
PingMe And Lobby Data
The PingMe / DCD lobby tools use forum thread, subscriber, and presence information to notify members
when a host's Among Us lobby reopens.
Stored Configuration
The bot may store server IDs, enabled forum channel IDs, forum thread IDs, thread owner user IDs,
whether DCD pings or lobby-open messages are enabled, subscriber user IDs waiting for a ping, and
optional thread emoji suffixes used when a thread is renamed.
Presence Information Used
When a tracked post owner has Discord activity available, the bot may read activity type, activity
name, state, and details. For Among Us activity, this can include whether the player is "In
Lobby," a lobby code, region, and host/lobby label exposed by Discord rich presence.
Runtime And Output
The bot may temporarily track recent lobby codes, requested thread names, cooldowns, and send
queues to avoid duplicate or rate-limited notifications. PingMe output may mention subscribed
members, post a lobby-open message, include the lobby code, or rename a forum thread using the
lobby code, host name, region, and configured emoji suffix.
Cleanup
Subscriber lists are cleared after a DCD reopen ping is sent or when a user removes themselves.
Thread state may remain while the feature is enabled for that post, while subscribers are waiting,
or while related thread settings are still active.
Storage And Access
Where Data Is Stored
Bot data may be stored in local databases, configuration files, logs, or other storage used to
operate the bot. Stored data may include moderation records, giveaway records, economy data,
game statistics, server settings, and user opt-in preferences.
Who Can Access It
Access is limited to authorized server staff, bot maintainers, or administrators who need the
information to operate, moderate, troubleshoot, or maintain the bot and server.
Retention And Deletion
Retention
Data is kept only as long as needed for bot functionality, server administration, moderation
history, audit logs, giveaways, game statistics, or abuse prevention.
Deletion Requests
Users may request deletion of eligible stored data. Some data may be retained when needed for
moderation history, safety, unresolved disputes, audit logs, or abuse-prevention requirements.
Sharing
No Sale Of Data
We do not sell user data. We do not share collected data with advertisers or unrelated third
parties.
Normal Server Visibility
Some bot output may be visible in server channels as part of normal functionality, such as
leaderboards, giveaway entries, public stats, role panels, event posts, or game participation
information.
Contact
For privacy questions, data requests, bot-related concerns, or priority support, contact the server
owner, admin email, or Priority Tickets channel.

admin@modded-au.org

Privacy Policy
This Privacy Policy explains information that may be processed when you connect to or use a custom Among Us

Information processed
To operate the region, the server may process technical, account, connection, and gameplay information, including:
IP addresses and network connection information.
Among Us player or account identifiers, including PUID-related information and friend codes where provided by the game.
Player names, game versions, platform or client information made available to the server.
Lobby information, game codes, player counts, game events, and server events.
Moderation, abuse-prevention, security, and diagnostic information.
Server logs generated while operating or troubleshooting the service.
How information is used
Information may be processed to:
Connect players and operate Among Us lobbies.
Maintain the availability, performance, and security of the regions.
Route connections between MAUL-operated region nodes.
Prevent abuse and enforce applicable MAUL rules.
Investigate crashes, connection problems, exploits, or other technical issues.
Diagnose and improve the reliability of the service.
Inter-node relay
MAUL operates regional server nodes. When inter-node relay is enabled for a lobby, information needed to
locate, register, and route that lobby may be exchanged between MAUL-operated nodes. Players connecting
through another MAUL node may have their game traffic relayed to the node hosting the lobby.
Logs & retention
Technical, security, moderation, and diagnostic logs may be retained when reasonably necessary to operate,
secure, troubleshoot, or maintain the service. Retention may vary depending on the information and why it
is needed.
Infrastructure
MAUL may use third-party hosting, networking, DNS, security, certificate, or infrastructure providers to
operate the regions. Those providers may process network or service information according to their own
terms and privacy practices.
Your choices
Connecting to a MAUL custom region is optional. If you do not want your information processed as described
here, do not connect to or use a MAUL-operated custom region.
Security
MAUL may use reasonable technical and operational measures intended to protect the region and information
processed by it. No internet-connected service can guarantee absolute security or uninterrupted operation.
Terms of Service
By connecting to or using a MAUL-operated custom Among Us region, you agree to these terms. If you do not
agree, do not use the region.
Use of the service
The regions are provided for custom and modded Among Us gameplay. You are responsible for how you use the
service and for following applicable MAUL rules and any rules established by a lobby host.
Prohibited use
You may not intentionally use the region to:
Attack, disrupt, overload, exploit, or interfere with the servers or other players.
Attempt unauthorized access to server systems, administrative functions, or other users' information.
Evade bans, technical restrictions, security controls, or abuse-prevention measures.
Use automation, malformed traffic, exploits, or other methods intended to damage or destabilize the service.
Use the service for unlawful activity.

EHR Template How-To
How to Use EHR Templates
Set up automatic lobby messages one step at a time. Start with the thing you want to do, copy an
example, then add timing, filters, variables, and placeholders only when you need them.
Home
Join Our Discord
What are you trying to make?
Search filters the guide as you type. Clear it to show everything again.
Pick Your Goal
Most people only need one of these patterns. Choose the closest one, copy it, and change the words.
Welcome Players
Greet each person as they join and include the room code, map, or Discord link.
See welcome examples
Send Reminders
Post lobby notifications, first-meeting notes, or meeting-specific instructions.
Choose a trigger
Target A Situation
Only send a message for certain maps, roles, ranks, lobby sizes, presets, or meetings.
Add bracket rules
Personalize Text
Use placeholders like player name, host name, map, player count, date, and time.
View placeholders
No matching guide items yet. Try a shorter word like "role", "map", "delay", or "welcome".
Start Here
If you have never made a template before, do this first. You can make more advanced templates later.
1
Open template.txt
This is where your lobby messages live. Each template starts on its own line with a tag.
2
Add a welcome
Paste welcome:Welcome to the lobby!. The word before the colon is the tag.
3
Save the file
Save your changes, then trigger the tag in game or let the automatic event happen.
4
Test it
Use /template welcome or /t welcome to send that template manually.
The simplest format is tag:message. You do not need brackets unless you want extra control.
Everything after the first colon is the message players will see.
Use clear tag names like welcome, rules, motd, or strategy.
Run /template with no arguments to list all available tags in the file.
You can press Enter to write a message across multiple lines. You no longer need \n, though it still works if you prefer it.
Template Words
These are the words people use when talking about templates. Once these click, the rest of the guide is much
easier to read.
Template File
The template.txt file is where every template entry lives. Save the file and EHR picks up the change next time it needs a template.
Tag
The tag is the name before the colon, like welcome or rules. Tags can use letters, numbers, and underscores.
Entry
An entry is one complete template block: the tag, optional bracket rules, the colon, and the message content.
Header
The header is the first line, shaped like tag[properties]: content. The brackets are optional.
Content
Content is the message EHR sends. It can be on the same line after the colon or on the lines below it.
Properties
Properties are bracket rules like map=Skeld, delay=5, hidden, or regex="^discord$".
Placeholder
A placeholder like {{PlayerName}} or {{RoomCode}} gets replaced with live game info when the message sends.
User Variable
A user variable is your own shortcut, like @discord = discord.gg/ehr. Use @discord later instead of typing the link again.
One tag can have multiple entries. That is how you make random choices, fallbacks, or different messages for different situations.
A hidden entry still works normally. It just does not show in the public /template list.
A regex trigger is different from a tag: the tag names the entry, while regex watches chat for text that should fire it.
What is the template file?
The template.txt file is the single text file where all your template data lives. This is
the file you edit to add or change any behavior.
<ModFolder>/EHR_DATA/template.txt
When you save changes, EHR picks them up the next time a matching event occurs. You usually do not need
to restart the game just because you changed a template.
What is the difference between a tag, entry, and template?
A tag is the name you give to a piece of content so EHR knows how to find and send it. Tags appear at
the start of a line, before the square brackets and colon.
greet[hidden]: Hello!
^^^^^
tag
An entry is one complete block of content in the template file. It starts with a tag and colon, and its
content is everything that follows until the next header appears.
Template is the general word people use for the whole system, or loosely for one entry or a group of
entries. When someone says "write a template for X", they usually mean "write an entry, or set of
entries, under a tag that handles X."
What are headers, content, and properties?
The header is the first line of an entry. It contains the tag, any properties, and optionally the start
of the content.
tag[properties]: content
Content is the actual message that gets sent when an entry is triggered. It is everything after the
colon on the header line, plus any extra lines below it until the next header.
Properties are optional conditions written inside square brackets. They control when and how an entry
behaves, like which map it applies to, how likely it is to be picked, whether it is hidden, or whether
it requires a chat message to match a regex pattern.
greet[map=Skeld, weight=3, hidden]: Hello from the Skeld!
Supported properties in plain English
Properties are optional conditions written inside the square brackets of a header. They control when and
how an entry behaves, things like which map it applies to, how likely it is to be picked, or whether it
requires a specific role.
map=Only send this entry on specific maps. Separate multiple maps with |, like map=Skeld|Polus.
meeting=Only send during a specific meeting number. Example: meeting=1 for the first meeting only.
role=Only send to players with a specific role. Prefix with ! to exclude a role, like role=!Impostor.
rank=Only send to players with a specific rank, such as Host, Admin, Mod, Moderator, or VIP.
players=Only send when the player count meets a condition, like players>=8 or players<=5.
preset=Only send when a specific game preset is active. Separate multiple presets with |.
weight=How likely this entry is to be picked when multiple entries share the same tag. Higher means more likely.
delay=Send this entry after a delay in seconds instead of immediately.
hiddenHide this tag from the public tag list. The entry still works normally.
regex=Only fire this entry when an incoming chat message matches the given pattern.
Multiple properties are separated by commas. Some properties are key=value pairs, while
hidden is just a key by itself. Its presence alone is enough to activate it.
What are placeholders, variables, and comments?
A placeholder is a special token written inside the content that gets replaced with a live value when
the message is sent.
announce: There are currently {{PlayerCount}} players in the lobby!
A user variable is a custom shorthand you define yourself with @name = value. Once defined,
you can write @name anywhere in your content and it gets substituted with the value you set.
@server = Endless Host Roles Official
welcome: Welcome to @server!
A comment is a line EHR ignores. Start the line with # when you want to leave yourself a
note or organize the file.
What are weighted picks, delayed entries, and cache?
When multiple entries share the same tag and at least one of them has weight=, EHR uses a
weighted pick to randomly choose one entry to send instead of sending all of them. Higher weight means
more likely to be chosen.
tip[weight=3]:Common tip.
tip[weight=1]:Rare tip.
A delayed entry is an entry with delay=. Instead of sending immediately, it waits the
specified number of seconds before the content is sent.
welcome:This sends right away.
welcome[delay=10]:This sends 10 seconds later.
Cache means EHR keeps a parsed copy of the template file in memory so it does not re-read and re-parse
the file on every single message. When the file changes, that parsed copy is rebuilt.
You do not usually need to think about cache. Just save your file and EHR will pick up the changes on
the next relevant event.
Choose When It Sends
Some tag names are automatic. Other tags are only sent when you run them manually.
Automatic system tags are triggered by the game. You do not call them yourself.
I want a message when someone joins
Use the welcome tag.
welcome:Welcome {{PlayerName}}! Code is {{RoomCode}}.
I want a repeating lobby reminder
Use the notification tag. The repeat timing comes from the auto-message settings.
Enable Auto-Message toggles the feature on or off.
The Auto-Message Is Sent Every X seconds controls how often it fires.
OnFirstMeeting:This is the first meeting. Crewmates, use the /myrole command to see your role info.
notification:{{PlayerCount}} players in lobby.
That example sends one first-meeting reminder and one repeating lobby notification.
I want a meeting message
Use OnMeeting for every meeting, or OnFirstMeeting for only the first one.
OnFirstMeeting:This is the first meeting. Use /myrole if you need your role info.
OnMeeting[meeting=2]:Second meeting. Start narrowing it down.
I want a message I can run myself
Make your own tag name, then trigger it with /template [tagname].
rules:Please read the lobby rules before joining voice.
To send it, run /template rules or /t rules.
Add Rules With Brackets
Brackets are optional. Use them when a message should only send in a specific situation.
Basic property syntax: tag[property=value]:message.
Multiple properties are separated by commas: tag[property=value, property=value]:message.
A template with no properties still works exactly as before. Properties are fully optional.
How do I delay a message?
Add delay=N, where N is 1-30 seconds. Delayed messages always send.
welcome:This sends right away.
welcome[delay=5]:This sends 5 seconds later.
welcome[delay=15]:This sends 15 seconds later.
How do I pick one random message?
Use the same tag more than once. Add weight=N if one should show more often.
motd[weight=8]:Remember to vote every meeting.
motd[weight=2]:Rare tip: check who is avoiding tasks.
Weights can be 1-10. Higher weight means that entry gets picked more often.
How do I send only on certain maps?
Use map=X. Separate multiple maps with |.
Valid map values are Skeld, MiraHQ, Polus, Airship, Fungle, and Dleks.
mapinfo[map=Skeld]:You are on Skeld!
mapinfo[map=Polus|Fungle]:You are on Polus or Fungle.
How do I send only to certain players?
Use role for in-game roles or rank for Host, Admin, Mod, Moderator, or VIP.
strategy[role=Jester]:Act suspicious, but survive long enough.
strategy[role=!Impostor]:You are not an Impostor. Work together and find them.
strategy:A generic tip for anyone else.
access[rank=Mod|Admin|Host]:Welcome, prestigious member!
You can add a fallback template with no role or rank condition for everyone else.
How do I check lobby size, preset, or meeting number?
Use players, preset, or meeting.
Player count supports >, >=, <, <=, =, and !=.
lobbysize[players>=15]:Big lobby! Starting soon.
lobbysize[players<6]:Still waiting for more players to join.
welcome[preset=2|3]:This message appears on Preset 2 or 3.
OnMeeting[meeting=3|4]:Meeting 3 or 4. Time is running out.
How do I hide a tag from the list?
Use hidden. The tag will not show in the /template listing, but it can still trigger.
ping[hidden]:Just an unfinished hidden message.
Regex Message Triggers
The regex property watches incoming chat messages and fires a template entry automatically when
the message matches. It is just a way to describe what a chat message should look like.
Template syntax: tag[regex="pattern"]:message.
A plain word works. regex="hello" matches messages that contain hello.
EHR checks the raw chat message and ignores uppercase/lowercase differences.
Use ^ and $ when you want the whole message to match exactly.
Backslashes should be doubled in template files, like \\b or \\d+.
Build an autoresponder
Fill this out to make a template that watches chat and answers automatically. The generated line can
go directly into template.txt.
Template name
This is the tag name. Use letters, numbers, or underscores.
Trigger word or phrase
This is what a player types in chat.
When should it trigger?
Only when the whole message matches
When the message contains this text
When this appears as its own word
When someone types it as a !command
When the message starts with this text
Hide from /template list
Useful for autoresponders because players trigger them by chat.
What should EHR say back?
discord.gg/maul
This is the response EHR sends when the trigger matches.
Generated template
What is regex?
Regex, short for regular expression, is a compact way to describe text. Instead of checking only one
exact sentence, you can describe patterns like "contains hello", "starts with !rules", "has a number",
or "says body as its own word."
For EHR templates, the pattern goes inside regex="...". When someone sends chat, EHR tests
that chat against the pattern. If it matches, the template sends.
rules[regex="^!rules$"]:Please read the lobby rules before the game starts.
Regex for dummies
Start with normal words, then add symbols only when you need more control.
hello
Matches any message containing hello.
^!rules$
Matches exactly !rules and nothing else.
^!settings
Matches messages that start with !settings.
thanks$
Matches messages that end with thanks.
body|report
Matches body or report anywhere in the message.
^(hi|hello)$
Matches exactly hi or exactly hello.
what.*role
Matches what, then anything, then role.
colou?r
Matches color or colour.
\\bbody\\b
Matches body as its own word, not somebody.
\\d+
Matches one or more numbers.
v1\\.0
Matches a literal dot, like v1.0.
How does EHR use it?
EHR reads every template with a regex property, compiles that pattern, then checks incoming
chat with it. If the pattern matches and any other bracket rules also pass, EHR sends the template.
help[regex="^!help$"]:Available commands: !rules, !discord, !settings
discord[regex="^!discord$"]:Join the Discord: discord.gg/maul
bodyhelp[regex="\\b(body|report|dead)\\b"]:
If you found a body, say where it was and who was nearby.
In practice, a player typing !discord triggers the Discord line. A player typing
where was body? triggers the body help line.
If you want the simplest autoresponder, make the word people type the regex and make the text after
the colon the answer.
discord[regex="^discord$"]:discordlink
That means: if someone says exactly discord, EHR replies with discordlink.
Replace discordlink with the real invite when you are ready.
Literal text and simple matches
The simplest pattern is just a word or phrase written out plainly. Spaces and punctuation are matched
literally unless they have a special meaning in regex.
rulecheck[regex="what are the rules"]:The rules are posted in the Discord!
By default, a pattern can match anywhere inside the message. So regex="hello" matches
hello, say hello to me, and hello everyone.
Quantifiers: how many times?
Quantifiers go right after whatever they apply to and control how many times it repeats. They are how
you say "optional", "one or more", or "exactly this many".
*Zero or more times. hel*o matches heo, helo, and hello.
+One or more times. hel+o matches helo and hello, but not heo.
?Zero or one time. colou?r matches both color and colour.
{4}Exactly 4 times. \\d{4} matches exactly 4 digits.
{2,8}Between 2 and 8 times.
{3,}3 or more times.
The combination .* is extremely common. It means "anything at all in between".
roleinfo[regex="what.*role"]:Check the role list with /roles!
Anchors: start and end of a message
Anchors pin a pattern to a specific position. Use them when you want to avoid accidental matches.
^Match must be at the very start of the message.
$Match must be at the very end of the message.
help[regex="^!help$"]:Here is the help menu.
settings[regex="^!settings"]:This fires when the message starts with !settings.
thanks[regex="thanks$"]:You are welcome!
Without anchors, regex="yes" can also fire on words like yesterday and
yessir. Anchors give you control.
Character sets: one of these characters
Square brackets define a set of acceptable characters at one position. The pattern matches if any one
character from the set is found there.
[aeiou]Any one vowel.
[a-z]Any lowercase letter.
[A-Z]Any uppercase letter.
[0-9]Any digit.
[a-zA-Z]Any letter, either case.
[a-zA-Z0-9_]Any letter, digit, or underscore.
gray[regex="gr[ae]y"]:Gray and grey both work.
code[regex="^[A-Za-z]{6}$"]:That looks like a 6-letter room code.
Put ^ as the first character inside the brackets to flip the meaning. For example,
[^0-9] means "anything except a digit".
OR, groups, and repeated text
Use | to say "this or that". Parentheses group parts of a pattern together so the choices
share the same anchors or repeat as one unit.
greet[regex="\\b(hi|hello|hey|sup|yo)\\b"]:Welcome to the lobby!
This catches any of those greeting words. Grouping matters: ^hi|hello$ means "starts with
hi OR ends with hello". Use ^(hi|hello)$ when you mean the entire message is exactly
hi or exactly hello.
laugh[regex="(ha)+"]:That is a lot of laughing.
good[regex="(very )*good"]:Glad to hear it.
Dots, numbers, words, and shortcuts
A dot . matches any single character: a letter, digit, symbol, space, anything. Shortcuts
describe common kinds of characters.
.Any single character.
.*Anything at all in between.
\\dAny digit, same as [0-9].
\\wAny word character: letters, digits, or underscore.
\\sAny whitespace, like a space or tab.
\\bA word boundary, useful for matching a word by itself.
roleinfo[regex="what.*role"]:Check the role list with /roles!
pin[regex="^\\d{4}$"]:That looks like a 4 digit PIN.
mention[regex="@\\w+"]:That looks like a player tag.
Inline flags
Flags go at the very start of your pattern inside (?...) and change how the pattern
behaves. EHR already ignores uppercase/lowercase differences, but these flags are useful to recognize
when testing or sharing patterns.
(?i)Case-insensitive. hello matches Hello, HELLO, and HeLLo.
(?m)Multiline. ^ and $ match the start and end of each line.
(?s)Dot-all. . can also match newline characters.
(?x)Extended. Spaces in the pattern are ignored and # starts a regex comment.
greet[regex="(?i)^\\b(hi|hey|hello|sup)\\b"]:Welcome to the lobby!
You can combine flags freely, like (?im). Most EHR templates will not need flags, but
knowing what they are makes examples from regex tools easier to read.
Escaping special characters
Some characters have special meaning in regex: . * + ? ^ $ { } [ ] | ( ) \. If you want
to match one of them literally, put a backslash in front of it.
A literal dot\\.
A literal question mark\\?
Literal parentheses\\(sus\\)
Three dots\\.\\.\\.
This is one of the most common mistakes: v1.0 means v1, then any character,
then 0. Use v1\\.0 when you mean the real dot in v1.0.
How do I combine regex with other rules?
Regex can sit next to other bracket rules. Separate properties with commas. This example only responds
to !settings on Preset 2 or 3.
settings[regex="^!settings$", preset=2|3]:
Current setup: {{Map}} | {{PlayerCount}} players | Preset {{Preset}}
You can also hide regex-triggered templates so they do not appear in the manual
/template list.
rules[regex="^!rules$", hidden]:
No slurs, no teaming, no stream sniping, and keep meetings readable.
Useful real examples
These are ready to copy and adjust.
# Respond to greetings
greet[regex="\\b(hi|hello|hey|sup|yo)\\b"]:Hey! Welcome to the lobby!
# Answer role questions
roleinfo[regex="what.*(role|roles)"]:Check the role list with /roles in chat!
# Share the room code when asked
roomcode[regex="(room ?code|what.s the code|how (do i|to) join)"]:The room code is {{RoomCode}}!
# Catch a message that is only 6 letters, like an Among Us room code
SelfPromo[regex="^[A-Za-z]{6}$"]:DO NOT ADVERTISE YOUR LOBBY HERE!
# Reply when someone types only a number
countdown[regex="^\\d+$"]:Numbers are not votes. Use the meeting buttons.
Quick regex reference
Use this when you remember what you want, but not the symbol for it.
helloThe word hello anywhere in the message.
^helloMessage starts with hello.
hello$Message ends with hello.
^hello$Entire message is exactly hello.
.Any single character.
\\.A literal dot.
\\wAny letter, digit, or underscore.
\\dAny digit 0-9.
\\sAny whitespace.
\\bWord boundary.
*Zero or more of the previous thing.
+One or more of the previous thing.
?Zero or one of the previous thing.
{4}Exactly 4 of the previous thing.
[a-z]Any lowercase letter.
[^0-9]Anything except a digit.
a|ba or b.
(abc)Group.
Common mistakes
Use quotes around the regex value: regex="^!rules$".
Double backslashes in regex shortcuts: write \\d+, not \d+.
Escape dots when you mean a real dot: write v1\\.0, not v1.0.
Use ^ and $ for commands so random sentences do not trigger them.
Group shared choices with parentheses: use ^(hi|hello)$, not ^hi|hello$.
Use | for "or", such as body|report|dead.
Keep broad patterns like .* rare because they match almost everything.
Testing tip: regex101.com is useful if you set the flavor to .NET. Remember to double backslashes again
when you paste the final pattern into template.txt.
Testing your patterns
Before adding a pattern to your template file, test it at regex101.com and set the flavor to .NET.
Paste in sample messages to see what matches and what does not. The site also explains what each part
of your pattern does, which is great for learning.
One EHR-specific reminder: this template parser stores doubled backslashes. If regex101 shows
\bdiscord\b, write \\bdiscord\\b in template.txt.
No matter how careful you are, broad patterns can still catch messages you did not expect. Test with
examples that should match and examples that should not match.
Reuse Text With Variables
Variables are handy for links, lobby summaries, and repeated lines you do not want to type over and over.
How do I make a variable?
Put the variable on its own line, then use it later with @name.
@discord = discord.gg/ehr
@session = {{Date}} | {{Time}}
@lobby = {{Map}} | {{PlayerCount}} players | Code: {{RoomCode}}
welcome:
@lobby
Join our server at @discord!
Placeholders inside variables are filled when the message sends.
What should I avoid?
Do not define variables in the middle of a message.
Do not put comments at the end of a template line.
Start comments on their own line with #. Comment lines are ignored entirely.
If a variable is not defined, it stays as-is in the final message.
# This is a comment
welcome: Greetings!
Copy-Friendly Examples
Start with one of these, then edit the message text for your lobby.
A simple welcome setup
@discord = discord.gg/ehr
@lobby = {{Map}} | {{PlayerCount}} players | Code: {{RoomCode}}
welcome:
Welcome {{PlayerName}}!
@lobby
Join our server at @discord!
A first-meeting reminder
OnFirstMeeting:
This is the first meeting.
Use /myrole if you need your role info.
Remember to vote before time runs out.
A big-lobby reminder
lobbysize[players>=15]:
Big lobby! Starting soon.
Please stay in lobby and avoid spam joining.
A map-specific tip
mapinfo[map=Polus|Fungle]:
This map has a lot of space.
Pay attention to where bodies are found and who was nearby.
A chat command that answers itself
rules[regex="^!rules$", hidden]:
Rules: no slurs, no teaming, no stream sniping, and keep meetings readable.
discord[regex="^!discord$", hidden]:
Join the lobby Discord: discord.gg/maul
Players can type !rules or !discord in chat and EHR will answer automatically.
discord[regex="^discord$", hidden]:discord.gg/maul
This version answers when someone types discord without the exclamation mark.
Full Template File Example
This small template.txt example puts most features together in one place.
@discord = discord.gg/ehr
# Welcome messages with weighted random pick
welcome[weight=7]:Welcome to {{HostName}}'s lobby! Join our Discord: @discord
welcome[weight=3]:Glad you joined! Find us at @discord
# Send a message 10 seconds after the welcome fires
welcome[delay=10]:Hope you have an unforgettable experience in my lobby!
# Auto-message shown in lobby every X seconds
notification:{{PlayerCount}} players | {{Map}} | Preset: {{Preset}}
# Chat command auto-responses
rules[regex="^!rules$", hidden]:No slurs, no teaming, no stream sniping, and keep meetings readable.
discord[regex="^!discord$", hidden]:Join the lobby Discord: @discord
# First meeting reminder
OnFirstMeeting:First meeting! Think before you vote.
# Target a specific meeting
OnMeeting[meeting=3]:Third meeting. Crewmates need to figure this out.
# Only show on big lobbies
OnMeeting[players>=12]:Big game with {{PlayerCount}} players. Stay focused.
# Role-specific tips
strategy[role=Jester]:You are the Jester. Get voted out to win.
strategy[role=!Impostor]:You are Crew. Find the Impostors!
strategy:Play smart and have fun.
# Rank-only template hidden from listing
ping[rank=Mod|Admin|Host, hidden]:Lobby check | {{PlayerCount}} players | {{Map}} | {{Time}}
Placeholders
Placeholders are wrapped in double braces and filled dynamically when a message is sent.
Player And Lobby
{{PlayerName}}Name of the receiving player
{{HostName}}Name of the current host
{{RoomCode}}Lobby join code
{{Map}}Name of the current map
{{PlayerCount}}Total players in the lobby
{{AlivePlayerCount}}Number of players currently alive
{{DeadPlayerCount}}Number of players currently dead
{{Players}}Names of all players, comma separated
{{AlivePlayers}}Names of alive players, comma separated
{{DeadPlayers}}Names of dead players, comma separated
Game Settings
{{KillCooldown}}Kill cooldown in seconds
{{DiscussionTime}}Discussion time in seconds
{{VotingTime}}Voting time in seconds
{{EmergencyCooldown}}Emergency button cooldown in seconds
{{NumEmergencyMeetings}}Emergency meetings allowed per player
{{PlayerSpeedMod}}Player speed multiplier
{{CrewLightMod}}Crewmate vision multiplier
{{ImpostorLightMod}}Impostor vision multiplier
{{NumCommonTasks}}Number of common tasks
{{NumLongTasks}}Number of long tasks
{{NumShortTasks}}Number of short tasks
Game State
{{MeetingCount}}Number of meetings held so far
{{GameDuration}}Elapsed game time as mm:ss
{{Preset}}Name of the active preset, such as Preset 1
Version And Time
{{AmongUsVersion}}Among Us version
{{InternalVersion}}EHR internal version number
{{ModVersion}}EHR display version
{{Date}}Current date
{{Time}}Current time
Troubleshooting
If a template does not send the way you expected, check these first.
It does not show in /template
Make sure the tag is not marked hidden. Hidden templates can still trigger, but they do
not show in the list.
The message does not send
Check the bracket rules. A map, role, rank, player count, preset, or meeting condition may not be met.
A variable appears as text
Make sure the variable is defined on its own line, like @discord = discord.gg/ehr.
Delay feels different than expected
Immediate entries go through weighted picks. Delayed entries always fire after their delay.
Made with reference to Zypherus' EHR template guide and code.

Community Features
The bot may be used for moderation, role management, verification-related workflows, giveaways,

Used when message text is needed for prefix commands, custom commands, autoresponders, sticky
messages, Mafia or game log parsing, chat activity tracking, economy rewards, moderation tools,
and other chat-based server features. Message content is used for bot functionality only.
Server Members Intent
Used to read member information needed for verification-related workflows, role panels, role
management, permission checks, moderation actions, warning systems, eligibility checks,
participation tracking, and member support tools.
Presence Intent
Used for features that depend on Discord activity status, especially Among Us rich presence. This
lets the bot detect when a tracked host appears to be in an open lobby, post lobby-open messages,
ping opted-in members, and show a user's current activity details through debug commands.
Default Discord Events
The bot also uses Discord's default event access for normal server operation, such as knowing
which servers, channels, threads, roles, messages, reactions, voice states, invites, emojis, and
interactions exist where the bot has permission. These events support commands, panels, logs,
reaction features, voice or lobby tools, and server automation.

PingMe And Lobby Data
The PingMe / DCD lobby tools use forum thread, subscriber, and presence information to notify members

Stored Configuration
The bot may store server IDs, enabled forum channel IDs, forum thread IDs, thread owner user IDs,
whether DCD pings or lobby-open messages are enabled, subscriber user IDs waiting for a ping, and
optional thread emoji suffixes used when a thread is renamed.
Presence Information Used
When a tracked post owner has Discord activity available, the bot may read activity type, activity
name, state, and details. For Among Us activity, this can include whether the player is "In

Runtime And Output
The bot may temporarily track recent lobby codes, requested thread names, cooldowns, and send
